grf.observed_anchor: The process request text can be immutable while Linux executable-path resolution remains late-bound at effect time.
grf.generated_reality: If path/argv immutability were sufficient executable provenance, the same immutable request would continue to identify the same executable across calls.
grf.counter_reality: Linux path lookup can resolve the same absolute path to a different executable after namespace/filesystem mutation, so request identity and executable identity are distinct.
grf.falsifier: Retarget one absolute executable symlink between two calls while keeping the exact argv tuple unchanged, then rollback and repeat.

unusual_experiment.name: SYMLINK_RETARGET_SAME_IMMUTABLE_ARGV
unusual_experiment.environment: isolated local sandbox; source-equivalent reconstruction of current-main host_process semantics, not claimed as exact private-repo blob execution
unusual_experiment.baseline: same immutable argv points through symlink to executable A and emits A
unusual_experiment.intervention: atomically retarget the same absolute symlink path to executable B without changing argv
unusual_experiment.predicted_if_hypothesis_right: same argv continues to execute A
unusual_experiment.predicted_if_counterhypothesis_right: same argv executes B because path resolution is late-bound
unusual_experiment.rollback: retarget symlink back to executable A; final control again executed A
